With demographic and family-history data, this yielded 59 features. Unified classifier-chain and single-label models were built with 5 algorithms across 6 modeling stages, evaluated with repeated nested cross-validation, and compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and paired bootstrap tests. title: TrialAgentBench: Evaluating AI Agents for Clinical-Trial Analysis and Long-Horizon Drug-Development Decisions
desc: Clinical drug development is a long-horizon, high-stakes process requiring sequential decisions based on information that costs money and time to acquire. AI agents have demonstrated capabilities for scientific analysis, but there is no established way to evaluate them on these decisions, as real trials are expensive, involve people, and never reveal the counterfactual. We introduce TrialAgentBench, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on clinical trial analysis and drug development decision-making using simulated trials where the truth is known, embedded within the data records of a fictional drug sponsor. We publicly release nearly 3,500 tasks, varying from analysing a single trial to managing multi-phase programmes with budget and time constraints. We score each analysis by rerunning its code on new trials, and each programme by the value its decisions achieve. Across 24 closed- and open-weight models, the strongest agents can analyse raw, messy trial records to within 6% of a process-aware analysis, even when an assumption is violated, with 95% confidence intervals containing the true effect 94--95% of the time. Over the prior year, the best model improved from 19% above this analysis, with serious misses on 15% of tasks, to 3.5% and 1%. What limits them is decision-making from evidence under uncertainty: when to correct, what evidence to buy, when to stop. The strongest agents are overly careful, correcting on 83% of tasks with equal recording errors, where it is unnecessary. On drug programmes, the best agent has substantial headroom, reaching 48% of the value an oracle achieves against 58% for a rule-based developer, with others falling 24 to 66% short. Model generations show ongoing improvements in handling data and evidence, with substantial variation. The strongest models can act as competent analysts, but do not yet make reliable long-horizon decisions.

Navigating Without a Compass: Chinese Medical Students' Perspectives on AI in Clinical Training.
desc: [Perspectives on medical education] Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming clinical practice, yet its integration into medical education remains largely unstructured. In China, where AI adoption is accelerating, little is known about how medical students perceive AI's role or what guidance they expect from educators. This study explores Chinese medical students' perspectives on AI in clinical training and their preferences for faculty engagement. Using educational cultural hegemony as a theoretical framework, the research team conducted in-depth, semi-structured interviews with 13 medical students across all five years of training at a medical school in China. Interviews addressed three sensitizing scenarios involving AI for clinical documentation, diagnostic assistance, and learning support. Transcripts were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis. Four themes were identified: Learning in the Shadows describes how students use AI covertly due to uncertain policies; Trust but Verify captures students' nuanced stance on AI reliability; The Human Element reveals concerns that AI may erode clinical reasoning and patient-physician relationships within China's high-volume healthcare system; and Educator as Compass describes students' desire for faculty who proactively teach AI literacy and model appropriate use. Chinese medical students navigate AI use without formal guidance in an ambiguous space between enthusiasm and caution. They seek educators who acknowledge AI's presence and preserve humanistic medicine. Findings underscore the urgent need for curricular integration of AI literacy and faculty development, particularly within hierarchical educational contexts. These findings carry implications beyond China's borders, suggesting that when institutions fail to acknowledge emerging technologies, students adapt independently but not necessarily safely or equitably.

title: Germline Variant Profiling of NA12878 Chromosome 22 Identifies the Loss-of-Function CYP2D6*3 and *4 Pharmacogenetic Alleles
desc: The approach used in this project to call germline variants from short-read sequencing data forms the basis of a great deal of current human genetics, whether it be in population studies or in diagnostic testing. A full germline variant-calling workflow according to the GATK Best Practices was constructed and carried out using public whole-genome sequencing data from the reference sample NA12878. In order to comply with the limitations of a laptop (an Intel Core i3, 8 GB of RAM, Ubuntu via WSL2), the analysis was limited to chromosome 22. The reads for chromosome 22 were streamed directly from the 1000 Genomes high-coverage CRAM file (run ERR3239334), converted into paired FASTQ files, checked using FastQC and MultiQC, and then cleaned with fastp. The cleaned reads were aligned to a GRCh38 reference containing only chromosome 22 using BWA-MEM, after which they were sorted, duplicates were marked and the base quality scores were recalibrated before variants were called with GATK HaplotypeCaller. The GATK-recommended hard filters were applied separately to SNPs and indels, and the variants that passed these filters were annotated using the Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor (VEP) and summarised with a Python script. From the 81,599 raw calls, 73,570 (90.2%) survived the filtering process, and the transition/transversion ratio for the SNPs that passed filtering was 2.04. Of the annotated variant alleles, 98.9% were already present in the catalogue, 734 affected the coding sequence in 270 genes, and no variant corresponded to a pathogenic entry in ClinVar. Examination using IGV verified the read support for the selected high-impact calls, including the variants that define the CYP2D6*3 and *4 alleles, consistent with the published genotype of NA12878. The main limitations were a reduced effective depth of 8.6x, resulting from an incomplete read-collation step which retained about 31% of the read pairs, and the use of a chromosome-only reference.

title: Foundation Model and Radiomics Distance Scores for Post-Hoc Segmentation Failure Detection
desc: Medical image segmentation models can fail silently when clinical data differs from training data. Deployed models rarely ship with quality control, and are often black boxes. Prior methods that work in this post-hoc failure detection setting still need a separate regression or segmentation model, registration, or access to model internals. We instead propose two failure scores based on the Mahalanobis distance to a labeled reference set. The first uses radiomic shape features of the predicted mask. The second uses frozen foundation model (FM) features, made mask-aware by overlaying the mask on the image, encoding it with a frozen DINOv3, and pooling patch features with more weight on the mask region. We test on multi-site prostate and hippocampus MRI under imaging-protocol and population shift. Ranking cases by predicted failure risk within each site, both scores are competitive with the registration-based (Atlas-RCA) and ensemble-based (pairwise Dice) baselines, without registration that can fail silently or access to individual predictions. Our results show that pooling all test cases into one ranking, as prior work does, rewards ordering sites by difficulty, so a detector can rank sites well, miss failures within them, and still look strong. Within-site evaluation measures true per-case failure. The two evaluation schemes reward different behavior, so we recommend reporting both. The code is available at https://github.com/imigraz/fm-radiomics-failure-detection.

title: SalivaryHSI-Seg: A New Challenging Benchmark for Ex Vivo Salivary Gland Hyperspectral Tissue Segmentation
desc: Salivary gland tumors are common lesions in oral and maxillofacial practice, and accurate identification of tumor regions and surrounding salivary gland tissues is important for tissue assessment, pathological sampling, and clinical decision support. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) records continuous spectral responses together with spatial imaging information, providing a promising way to capture fine-grained tissue-discriminative information. Nevertheless, the development of salivary gland HSI tissue segmentation remains limited due to the lack of standardized benchmarks with pixel-level annotations and unified evaluation protocols. To address this issue, we introduce SalivaryHSI-Seg, a hyperspectral tissue segmentation benchmark for ex vivo salivary gland specimens, containing 119 HSI samples from 31 patients with multi-class pixel-level annotations. We establish a patient-level five-fold cross-validation protocol and evaluate different input representations, model architectures, and challenging subsets with small tumor and complex boundary. Based on this benchmark, we further propose HyBSD, a hyperspectral boundary-guided spectral-difference network for full-HSI salivary gland tissue segmentation. HyBSD exploits boundary-guided spectral-difference cues to improve tissue delineation in ambiguous transition regions. Extensive experiments show that full-HSI input provides more discriminative information than sampled spectrums, and that HyBSD achieves 74.97% mDice and 87.76% Tumor Dice, with further advantages on the challenging subsets. Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Natural Product Pharmacology: From Molecular Discovery to Precision Therapeutics.
desc: [Pharmacological research] The use of natural products as a chemically diverse source of bioactive molecules for drug development has been well established; however, their multicomponent and multitarget nature, uncertain target causality, variable in vivo exposure, and heterogeneous responses to therapy make them challenging to characterize pharmacologically and translate into clinical practice. Systems pharmacology, together with artificial intelligence (AI), provides new approaches for molecular screening, target prioritization, integration of multidimensional data, and development of precision therapeutics. Osteoarthritis (OA), a heterogeneous whole-joint disease characterized by inflammation, oxidative stress, metabolic dysfunction, and tissue remodeling, serves as a representative model for evaluating such approaches. Network pharmacology can be used to organize relationships among natural product constituents, disease-related targets, and signaling pathways. AI can further assist with activity prediction, compound and target prioritization, multi-omics integration, and patient stratification. Studies combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, deep-learning-based affinity prediction, and experimental validation to narrow the list of potential candidate constituents and targets demonstrate the utility of computational methods in candidate prioritization. This article describes the transition of natural product pharmacology from empirical discovery and systems-based analysis to AI-enabled molecular discovery, mechanistic interpretation, pharmacokinetic assessment, and precision therapeutics. Although computational approaches may facilitate the identification and prioritization of biologically active constituents and targets, they remain limited by uncertainty regarding causality, inadequate in vivo exposure, model dependence, and insufficient clinical evidence. Future studies should focus on precise active-compound identification, direct target validation, systematic pharmacokinetic assessment, and high-quality clinical research to enhance the reliability and translational value of AI-enabled natural product pharmacology.

title: Differential Proteomics to XAI Rules: A SHAP-FOL-ILP Modeling for Lung Adenocarcinoma
desc: Background: We developed an interpretable workflow linking paired differential proteomics, sparse logistic regression, SHAP attribution, and first-order logic (FOL) rule learning in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Methods: We analysed 213 CPTAC-LUAD tissue samples (111 tumour, 102 adjacent-normal) from 111 patients, including 102 matched pairs. Protein effect estimation and testing used the same complete pairs, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Sparse logistic regression used five-fold stratified patient-grouped nested cross-validation. Preprocessing and model selection were confined to training data, with feature selection repeated within inner folds. A separate five-fold patient-grouped evaluation tested SHAP-guided inductive logic programming (FOL/ILP) using training-derived evidence and discretisation. Results: Quality control retained 9,518 proteins. At FDR below 0.05 and an absolute mean paired log-ratio difference of at least 1, 378 were differentially abundant (40 increased, 338 decreased). The sparse classifier yielded ROC-AUC 0.9997, average precision 0.9998, accuracy 0.9906, and balanced accuracy 0.9906. FOL/ILP yielded held-out accuracy 0.9765, balanced accuracy 0.9767, precision 0.9818, recall 0.9730, and F1 0.9774. HSPA12B, PALM2-AKAP2, STARD13, and PPM1F had non-zero coefficients in all five classifier folds. The most frequent Horn clause occurred in two of five folds. All others occurred once. Conclusions: The workflow connects proteomic classification, attribution, and symbolic rules. Performance reflects tumour-versus-adjacent-normal discrimination within one cohort. Biomarker and clinical claims require independent validation, repeated assessment of rule stability, and further biological annotation.

The arc of uncertainty across clinicians' interactions with AI.
desc: [Discover artificial intelligence] Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used in various clinical settings to support clinical reasoning and decision-making. Although they have demonstrated strong performance on medical knowledge and reasoning tasks, and early studies suggest potential to reduce medical errors, emerging evidence also highlights important safety concerns, including clinically significant management errors in outputs that may not be readily apparent to users. How these tools can be integrated into clinical practice to consistently lead to improved patient outcomes remains an open question. AI-assisted reasoning unfolds across a sequence of decisions: whether to use AI for the clinical question, how to engage with the tool, how to interpret its output, and whether to act. Each stage in this sequence introduces distinct risks, including inappropriate tool selection, incomplete or biased inputs, overconfidence in fluent responses, and failure to recognize error or appreciate nuance. These risks are further shaped by the same clinician factors that generally affect clinical reasoning such as experience, workload, and uncertainty management. Viewing the AI-clinician interaction as a process rather than a single moment highlights several key points of vulnerability but also opportunities for training. Ultimately, the safe use of AI may depend less on the quality of the model and more on the clinician's ability to recognize when its outputs should be questioned, verified, or set aside.

title: Separating Genetic and Protein Evidence in Open Targets: An Auditable Re-ranking Study
desc: Biomedical target-ranking platforms combine genetics, literature, experimental evidence, tractability, and clinical precedent because each is useful for target discovery. A single integrated score, however, can be awkward to reuse for a narrower question such as which genes have direct evidence for disease risk or etiology. We examine this issue in Open Targets associations for Alzheimer disease (AD) and Parkinson disease (PD). Genetics-linked evidence and protein-oriented evidence are scored in separate channels and combined only at the end. In AD, the Open Targets overall top 20 contains 7 curated genetics-supported genes and 10 symptomatic pharmacology controls; the default late fusion contains 15 curated genes and no symptomatic controls. In PD, late fusion retains 13 curated genes and removes the 5 symptomatic controls present in the platform top 20. A genetics-only ranking reaches similar curated recall (14 genes in AD, 13 in PD), so most of the gain over the platform score comes from emphasizing genetic evidence; the protein channel mainly raises the number of tractable targets in the shortlist (from 9 to 12 in AD and from 8 to 10 in PD) without readmitting symptomatic controls. These results are stable across fusion weights from 0.35 to 0.75, perturbed protein-channel weights, and rule thresholds. An optional post-ranking rule further lowers high-clinical/low-genetic targets such as ACHE and GRIN1 without changing top-20 curated recall. The procedure is deterministic and uses public Open Targets fields. Because the component scores remain available, individual rank changes can be inspected and the ranking can be reproduced from the same data snapshot.

title: AI医疗商业化进入深水区：医渡科技能否跑通医院与药企两端？-证券之星
Designing large language model tutors to promote deep learning and precision medical education.
source: PubMed · Academic medicine : journal of the Association of American Medical Colleges
desc: [Academic medicine : journal of the Association of American Medical Colleges] The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) by medical students has created two significant concerns: that students will use artificial intelligence (AI) for quick answers, short-circuiting the cognitive effort essential for deep learning, and that the satisfaction of discovery will be lost to algorithmic efficiency. This Scholarly Perspective reframes LLMs not as information retrieval systems, but as "Socratic Mirrors": interactive tutors grounded in established learning science (such as the desirable level of difficulty, social constructivism and zone of proximal development, the illusion of explanatory depth, and dual coding theory) that can restore the productive struggle that traditional LLMs often constrain. Drawing on the three functions of education framework, the authors argue that by handling qualification (the foundational work of content mastery), Socratic tutors free faculty to focus on what AI cannot provide: socialization (initiation into the norms and values of the profession) and subjectification (the formation of physicians as autonomous, ethical, and reflective practitioners). This potential is not merely theoretical. Empirical evidence from randomized controlled trials suggests that pedagogically engineered AI tutors, those designed to scaffold discovery rather than deliver answers, can significantly outperform traditional instruction. The studies demonstrate how LLMs configured as Socratic tutors can address the "2-Sigma" problem, offering personalized one-on-one tutoring at scale and moving medical education closer to the ideal of precision education. However, these studies are drawn from outside medical education, and the inferential leap to medical training, while theoretically grounded, remains empirically undemonstrated. The PICRAT (passive, interactive, creative, replacement, amplification, transformation) model is presented as a technology integration framework to ensure intentional rather than reactive AI integration. Together, these principles suggest a promising pathway toward scalable precision medical education that warrants formal evaluation in medical education contexts.

title: A Cascaded Framework with a Cross-Attention-Guided Mamba-CNN Model for Pre- and Post-Treatment Glioma Segmentation
desc: Accurate glioma segmentation is vital for diagnosis and follow-up, but manual segmentation is time-consuming, subjective, and variable across interpreters. Gliomas are heterogeneous in size, shape, and location. Deep learning has therefore emerged as a potential solution. CNNs excel at local features but may struggle with long-range dependencies, whereas Vision Transformers capture global context efficiently but incur higher computational complexity. Most previous studies focused on pre-treatment gliomas; post-treatment cases with resection cavities (RCs) remain less explored. This study proposes a Cross-Attention-Guided Mamba-CNN (CMC-Seg) model within a cascaded framework for pre- and post-treatment diffuse glioma segmentation, aiming to balance accuracy and computational cost. Experiments used BraTS 2025 mpMRI of diffuse glioma patients. After preprocessing, a coarse segmentation model extracted tumor-centered patches, which were fed to CMC-Seg for fine-grained segmentation. CMC-Seg was compared with 3D U-Net, SegResNet, SwinUNETR, UNETR, nnFormer, and SegMamba. On the test set, CMC-Seg achieved the highest mean Dice (81.20%) and non-enhancing tumor core (NETC) Dice (77.09%). It also achieved an RC Dice of 78.63% and the lowest 95% Hausdorff distance (HD95; 4.39 mm). Results were comparable to CNN and Mamba baselines and significantly better than Transformer-based baselines (P < 0.05). CMC-Seg required the fewest inference GFLOPs (381.49). Ablation experiments indicated that multi-direction scanning and cross-attention improved performance, particularly for RC (P < 0.05). Grad-CAM explainability experiments showed that CMC-Seg focuses on diagnostically relevant tumor regions.

title: 蚂蚁百灵医疗健康大模型宣布开源
AI-based histopathologic grading for predicting biochemical recurrence in prostate cancer.
desc: [BJU international] Our objective was to evaluate artificial intelligence (AI)-based Gleason grading of prostate cancer (PCa) biopsies compared with expert pathologist-based consensus grading and clinical risk factors for predicting biochemical recurrence (BCR) after radical prostatectomy. Although Gleason grading is the most validated prognostic factor in PCa, interobserver variability may affect its prognostic accuracy, particularly for intermediate-risk tumours and non-subspecialty pathologists. Whole-slide images from PCa biopsy specimens were analysed in patients originally diagnosed with grade group (GG)-2 PCa by general pathologists; patients subsequently underwent radical prostatectomy (n = 217). A representative biopsy slide containing up to two cores was analysed per case. Gleason scores were re-assigned by consensus among three genitourinary pathologists or by AI model. Cox proportional hazards models were constructed using CAPRA (Cancer of the Prostate Risk Assessment) score, percent pattern 4 (%p4), and cribriform/intraductal carcinoma, derived from either pathologist consensus or AI-based grading. Discrimination was described with Harrell's C-index; the pathologist-based and AI-based multivariable models were formally compared using Uno's C-statistic, 3- and 5-year time-dependent area under the curve, and Akaike information criterion. In total, 35 patients (16%) had BCR. In univariable models, AI-based GG had a numerically higher C-index than consensus pathologist GG (0.66 vs 0.61). Similarly, CAPRA score incorporating AI-based GG (AI-CAPRA) had a numerically higher C-index than that incorporating consensus-pathologist GG (pathologist-CAPRA) (0.68 vs 0.65). In multivariable models, AI-detected cribriform/intraductal carcinoma independently predicted an increased risk of BCR when combined with AI-CAPRA and AI %p4 (hazard ratio 2.97; 95% confidence interval 1.11-7.91), whereas neither pathologist-detected cribriform/intraductal carcinoma nor pathologist-detected %p4 was independently prognostic when combined with pathologist-CAPRA. AI-based Gleason grading had prognostic performance similar to that of expert pathologist consensus grading, alone or combined with clinical variables. AI-detected (but not pathologist-detected) cribriform/intraductal carcinoma had independent prognostic value in multivariable models with CAPRA score. These findings support a role for AI-assisted pathology in PCa risk stratification, particularly in settings without subspecialty genitou

title: Beyond Language Optimization: Enhancing Visual Representations for Radiology Report Generation
desc: Accurate chest X-ray radiology report generation (RRG) requires recognizing clinically relevant abnormalities and accurately describing them. Although Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves the clinical accuracy of generated reports, our analyses suggest limited improvements in visual representations for abnormality recognition. To address this limitation, we propose a selective regional visual distillation framework that enhances visual representations of challenging abnormalities while preserving existing visual capabilities. Specifically, we train a region-aware teacher with targeted supervision on challenging anatomical regions to acquire complementary visual knowledge. Rather than transferring all teacher features, we verify their utility through regional feature replacement and select only those that improve the original student's performance. We further introduce a Spatially Gated Residual Adapter (SGRA) to distill these verified features while minimizing interference with the student's existing visual representations. Experiments on MIMIC-CXR and IU-Xray demonstrate improved clinical report accuracy and region-level abnormality recognition across different multimodal large language model backbones, while largely preserving performance on non-target findings.

title: 钟南山院士谈医疗AI：助手而非替代者，决策者仍是医生
Generative Deep Learning for Computational Destaining and Restaining of Unregistered Digital Pathology Images.
source: PubMed · Proceedings of the ... International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications. International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications
desc: [Proceedings of the ... International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications. International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications] Conditional generative adversarial networks (cGANs) have enabled high-fidelity computational staining and destaining of hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) in digital pathology whole-slide images (WSI). However, their ability to generalize to out-of-distribution WSIs across institutions without retraining remains insufficiently characterized, limiting scalable clinical translation. Previously developed cGAN models trained on 102 registered prostate core biopsy WSIs from Brigham and Women's Hospital were evaluated on 82 spatially unregistered WSIs from three Stanford University patients. To mitigate domain shift without retraining, a preprocessing pipeline consisting of histogram-based stain normalization for H&E-stained WSIs and channel-wise intensity calibration for unstained WSIs was developed. Because image registration was intentionally omitted for real-world deployment conditions, the reported quantitative results are conservative lower bounds reflecting both model performance and limited spatial alignment. Under these conditions, virtual destaining achieved a Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.854, structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.699, and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 18.41 dB. H&E restaining from computationally destained outputs outperformed direct staining from ground-truth unstained inputs across all metrics (PCC: 0.798 vs. 0.715; SSIM: 0.756 vs. 0.718; PSNR: 20.08 vs. 18.51 dB), suggesting that preprocessing quality may be more limiting than model capacity. Qualitative pathological review indicated that benign glandular structures were more reliably preserved, and malignant glands were often rendered with vessel-like morphologies. These findings support the feasibility of applying cGAN-based computational H&E staining and destaining generative models to external WSI datasets using preprocessing-based adaptation alone, and identify malignant gland preservation for future domain adaptation.

title: MISeg-Agent: A Human-in-the-Loop Agentic Framework for Error Diagnosis and Executable Prompt Review in 3D Medical Image Segmentation
desc: Despite the strong performance of modern medical image segmentation models, their predictions can still contain localized errors that compromise segmentation quality. Identifying and correcting these errors is therefore essential for improving the reliability of existing segmentation results. While interactive segmentation models enable targeted corrections, identifying potential errors, determining where to intervene, and evaluating corrective actions remain challenging. Moreover, each correction changes the current mask, requiring subsequent error diagnosis and recommendations to adapt accordingly. To address these challenges, we propose MISeg-Agent, a human-in-the-loop agentic framework that diagnoses segmentation errors and provides evidence-based correction recommendations. MISeg-Agent first selects a suitable pretrained segmentation model based on benchmark performance and computational requirements. Given its predicted mask, the framework identifies potential missing and excess foreground regions and recommends suspicious slices and corrective points for review. The framework then evaluates candidate point prompts using an interactive segmentation model and presents the resulting corrections for human verification before applying them. By operating directly on images and predicted masks, the error diagnosis process remains independent of the underlying segmentation model architecture. Evaluations on CT datasets demonstrate that MISeg-Agent improves initial segmentation results and produces final masks closely aligned with reference annotations. By integrating adaptive error diagnosis with validated correction recommendations, MISeg-Agent provides an interpretable approach to identifying and reducing residual errors in existing medical image segmentations.

title: 蚂蚁集团开始开放发布 LingSante 医疗 AI 模型权重
Artificial Intelligence Series: Data Modalities and Clinical Applications in Rhinoplasty.
source: PubMed · Facial plastic surgery & aesthetic medicine
desc: [Facial plastic surgery & aesthetic medicine] Rhinoplasty requires individualized decisions that balance nasal appearance, airway function, structural support, and patient expectations. This narrative review examines artificial intelligence (AI) applications across the data modalities encountered in rhinoplasty care, emphasizing their potential roles in assessment, counseling, surgical planning, and outcome evaluation. Relevant modalities include clinical text, structured clinical data, facial photographs, anatomical imaging and three-dimensional surface geometry, and specialized measurements of surgical technique, nasal function, and visual perception. Clinical applications include patient counseling, organization of clinical records, risk and outcome prediction, quantitative nasal assessment, visualization of proposed changes, and postoperative evaluation. Multimodal and agentic systems may integrate these sources and tasks. Limitations include measurement errors, uncertain prediction of surgical outcomes, and limited evidence of improved clinical decisions or patient outcomes. Matching clinical questions to available data provides a practical framework for AI research and application in rhinoplasty. Standardized acquisition, secure linkage of longitudinal records, and independent validation are needed to support reproducible assessment and outcomes research. Surgeon oversight remains essential, with clinical value judged by functional and aesthetic outcomes and alignment with patient goals.

title: SAE-Audit: Clinical-Trial Prediction via Inference-Time Optimization of Black-Box LLMs Audited by Sparse Autoencoder Evidence
desc: Clinical trials are costly and often take years to complete, making early outcome prediction valuable for trial planning. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to forecast clinical-trial outcomes, yet their predictions remain unreliable and their rationales may not faithfully reflect the evidence underlying their answers. On tasks such as predicting whether a registered clinical trial will complete or terminate early, frontier LLMs perform only modestly above chance in our experiments. We introduce SAE-Audit, which optimizes a black-box LLM at inference time with evidence obtained from a deployable open model. A frozen sparse autoencoder (SAE) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is converted into a vocabulary of clinical concepts. Sparse probes fitted on past trials determine which concepts are associated with the outcome. For a new protocol, the concepts detected by the probe are written as evidence, each with the direction and strength of its association with the outcome, and the LLM being audited optimizes its answer in the light of this evidence. Without additional training, SAE-Audit raises balanced accuracy of deepseek-v4-flash by 9.6--12.0 points on five clinical-trial prediction tasks and raises GPT-5.6-terra by 8.0 points on trial completion, exceeding other agentic inference-time optimization methods by a large margin. As an auxiliary, SAE probes module within SAE-Audit is itself accurate and auditable, providing natural-language explanations directly derived from verified concept contributions and protocol evidence, without requiring additional LLMs at inference time. SAE-Audit provides verifiable, concept-level evidence for more accurate and auditable clinical-trial prediction. It can also be embedded into biomedical AI agents such as Biomni to optimize their performance.

title: 医疗AI初创公司Boltz获1.1亿美元融资，加速小分子药物研发-AI应用
Artificial intelligence predictive medicine: geometric morphometrics in assisted scoliosis diagnosis.
source: PubMed · European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
desc: [European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society] Accurate scoliosis screening is essential for early intervention and to minimize unnecessary exposure to radiographic imaging. This study presents a landmark-based approach using Geometric Morphometric Methods combined with Elastic Net regression for the automated, non-invasive detection of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from 3D torso surface scans. A retrospective cross-sectional study was performed on 168 individuals (135 with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and 33 controls) using automatic landmark extraction on surface meshes from previous studies. After dimensionality reduction via principal component analysis, the resulting shape variables were used to train a logistic regression model with regularization. The main outcome measures were Area Under the Curve, sensitivity, specificity and balanced accuracy to estimate the performance metrics of the Artificial Intelligence screening model. The model showed high discriminative ability on an unseen test dataset (Area Under the Curve = 0.926; 95% CI: 0.816-1.000). When a classification threshold derived exclusively from the training set was applied to the test set, sensitivity was 100%, specificity was 14.3%, and balanced accuracy was 57.1%. In contrast to deep learning models, this approach offers an interpretable framework based on anatomical landmarks and does not require large datasets or extensive computational resources. The findings support further investigation of surface trunk morphology as a source of discriminative information for AIS detection. External validation in larger and more representative populations is required before clinical screening application.

title: TesseraFlow: Scalable Video Diffusion for Dynamic Medical Imaging Inverse Problems
desc: Generative priors are state-of-the-art for modeling medical images in image reconstruction tasks, but reconstruction with video priors takes tens of seconds to minutes per frame. Latent priors inherit the errors of their autoencoder, the memory of pixel-space whole-frame priors grows with the frame size, and pixel-space patch priors are slow for two reasons. First, their deep networks process every frame at full resolution at every sampling step, even though early steps resolve only low frequencies. Second, their samplers spend many network evaluations per sampling step on overlapping windows, multiple re-noising rounds, or backpropagation through the prior. We introduce TesseraFlow, a complex-valued pixel-space flow prior that reduces the first cost. A global encoder reads a low-resolution view of every frame once per sampling step. A single shallow decoder operates on this view during early steps and on full-resolution space-time tiles during later steps, so no network processes a whole frame at full resolution. Our sampler, ReTile, addresses the second reason. We use randomized grid shifting at every sampling step along with re-noising, which acts as a stochastic gradient instead of computing overlapping tiles, so a single network pass per sampling step suffices. On its own, ReTile speeds up an existing global-context patch prior by 6-9x, and our prior adds a further 3-5x speedup. TesseraFlow reconstructs about one 256x256 frame per second, 20-367x faster than patch and latent video priors, and can match or exceed the best generative baseline on cardiac, brain, and abdominal MRI and lung CT, at a fraction of its GPU time.

title: Automated tool support for brain tumor diagnosis with explainability using MRI images.
desc: [Computational biology and chemistry] Precise and early detection of brain tumors is very important for successful clinical decision making. However the prevailing models didn't perform well on noisy images, also they didn't perform feature extraction to gather relevant tumor information. Most of the existing models produce good detection results with high complex architecture, increasing computational expensive. Moreover, these models have less interpretability and lacking accurate tumor detection, decreasing clinical decision making capability. To solve these issues, lightweight deep learning (DL) models is proposed in this research for accurate tumor segmentation and classification. This system include phase's namely pre-processing, segmentation, feature extraction, classification, model optimization and explainability. Experimental results are conducted on BraTS 2020 and BraTS 2018 datasets, proposed model produced accuracy of 99.75%, and 99.5% respectively.

title: CLASP: Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling for Zero-Shot OOD Detection using Vision-Language Models
desc: Vision-language models (VLMs) enable zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in medical imaging, yet existing approaches often rely on final-layer confidence or entropy-based layer selection, potentially missing complementary information. We show that low in-distribution (ID) confidence entropy does not reliably predict OOD discrimination. We introduce CLASP (Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling), an ID-only framework that jointly models layer--prompt responses and visual features. CLASP ranks visual encoder layers using Gaussian conditional mutual information and selects a compact subset through anchored spectral selection, without fixing the number of layers. It then combines the selected layer--prompt profiles with PCA-compressed visual embeddings and fits a single shrinkage-regularized Gaussian. OOD scores are computed using squared Mahalanobis distance, without fine-tuning, OOD training data, or test-time adaptation. Across histopathology, chest X-ray, and brain MRI benchmarks with UniMedCLIP and BioMedCLIP, CLASP performs strongly under varied distribution shifts. On MIDOG near-OOD, it achieves 87.54% AUROC with UniMedCLIP, outperforming confidence-based baselines; with BioMedCLIP, it remains competitive but trails visual-only Mahalanobis modeling. Ablations highlight the value of layer--prompt interactions and cross-feature dependencies, while exposing shift-dependent contributions and limitations under semantic shifts.

title: Large Language Model-Powered AI-Assisted Simulated Patient for Nursing Education: Quasi-Experimental Study.
desc: [JMIR nursing] Large language model (LLM)-powered virtual patient systems are gaining popularity in nursing education but also face persistent challenges, such as hallucinations and role inconsistency. This paper reports the model architecture design, technical considerations, implementation challenges, and evaluation of an LLM-powered AI-assisted simulated-patient system integrated into a nursing triage simulation game. The system integrated a Unity-based game client, with GPT-4o hosted through Microsoft AI Foundry to support real-time simulated-patient dialogue in Traditional Chinese using Cantonese syntax. This developmental study comprised exploratory model selection, formative student feedback-informed enhancement from Version 1 to Version 2, development-stage script-fidelity evaluation, and evaluation of system usability and the Net Promoter Score in 2 tutorial cohorts of nursing students. Key technical contributions include a layered hallucination mitigation architecture that combines grounded prompt inclusion, few-shot conversational exemplars, negative role constraints, and calibrated model parameters. In the predefined script-fidelity evaluation, script-inconsistent responses occurred in 78 of 125 (62.4%) Version 1 outputs and 21 of 125 (16.8%) Version 2 outputs-an absolute difference of 45.6 percentage points. The implementation process also addresses stateless API memory management, cloud-based safety filter calibration for domain-specific clinical prompts, and prompt engineering strategies to prevent role drift and hidden scenario information leakage. GPT-4o was selected as the production model through exploratory development testing that considered script consistency, Cantonese-language suitability, response latency, technical reliability, deployment feasibility, cost considerations, and Unity integration compatibility; 45 of 50 (90%) assessed GPT-4o responses were rated fully script-consistent. This study demonstrates the development and real-world tutorial deployment of a Cantonese-language, LLM-powered simulated-patient system for nursing triage education. Integrating formative student feedback with structured technical debugging enabled iterative refinement of dialogue fidelity, role consistency, protected-information handling, and game interaction functions. The resulting Version 2 system provides a practical, contextually tailored approach to supporting scalable simulated-patient dialogue in nursing education.

title: Who Gets Re-ranked When a Clinical Model Gains New Data?
desc: Hospitals often update a deployed risk model by adding a data source, such as laboratory results, that only some patients have. Work on safe model updates assumes fixed inputs and so ignores patients who lack the new data. The update has no new measurements for them, yet their rank can change, and a sick patient not yet tested can drop off an alert list. We split rank-based compatibility by data availability and pair it with error correction and alert-list effects. We compared each update with ordinary retraining on the old inputs, predicting ICU admission or death and hospital admission, on 78,475 emergency department visits from MC-MED and, in a pre-registered replication, 100,000 stays from MIMIC-IV-ED at a second hospital. Radiograph report text gave no detectable gain and almost no extra re-ranking. Laboratory results improved prediction but, at both hospitals and with linear or tree models, pushed patients without labs down alert lists; linear updates also reshuffled them more than retraining did, without ranking them better. A top-20% admission list caught 4.2% of admitted patients without labs after the update, against 18.8% after retraining (second hospital: 4.9% against 22.6%), while catching more patients overall. This held for list sizes from 5% to 50% and in every patient group we checked, despite better measured calibration. Separate alert thresholds for patients with and without labs restored most or all of their catch rate at both hospitals at almost no cost. Teams should check these patients before deploying such an update.

title: Development and Validation of an Artificial Intelligence-Driven Multigene Assay Decision-Support System for Personalized Management of T1 High-Grade Bladder Cancer.
desc: [MedComm] T1 high-grade bladder cancer presents a therapeutic dilemma, as current risk stratification fails to guide the choice between early cystectomy and bladder-preserving therapy. In our recent work, we defined a high-risk multiomic subtype driven by anoikis resistance and immune evasion and developed the T1HG-UCBguider framework for risk stratification; however, its reliance on multiomic sequencing limits clinical implementation. Here, we translate this framework into Guider, an artificial intelligence-driven reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) decision-aid designed for cost-conscious use in routine pathology workflows and integrating a 30-gene TaqMan assay with clinicopathological variables to predict progression and recurrence, with exploratory treatment-context modules for no instillation, Bacillus Calmette-Guérin, and intravesical chemotherapy. In a multicenter ambispective cohort of 1198 patients, Guider achieved > 10% higher absolute predictive performance than guideline-based risk groups and the published 12-gene progression score within this Chinese T1 high-grade cohort. Reclassification identified 82.5% of guideline-defined high-risk patients who progressed and 45.1% of very-high-risk nonprogressors who might be considered for bladder preservation. Guider could potentially support treatment de-escalation in 29.7% and escalation in 12.9% of patients. These findings establish a scalable translational framework bridging multiomic discovery and clinical decision support, warranting prospective interventional validation in geographically, ethnically, and demographically diverse populations.

title: Learning Multimodal Representations from Partially Paired, Small-Scale Data
desc: Modeling multimodal data from partially paired samples is critical for advancing domains like biomedicine, where vast unimodal datasets and foundation models exist but paired data remains scarce. Existing fusion methods rely on large-scale paired datasets, limiting their use in scenarios with incomplete pairing. We introduce CAMEO, an adversarial learning-based modality fusion framework that integrates modalities from small, partially paired datasets. Combining any pre-trained unimodal encoder with a cross-modal latent alignment mechanism, CAMEO learns shared representations requiring only minimal paired samples. Evaluated on computational pathology tasks such as niche classification and cell type composition prediction, CAMEO achieves superior data efficiency, outperforming contrastive approaches like CLIP in low paired-data regimes, and highlighting the benefits of adversarial alignment when paired annotations are scarce. To facilitate further research, we additionally release a fully annotated HuggingFace dataset comprising three organs and paired image and gene expression modalities. By extending fusion methods to address limited pairing and small-scale datasets, we provide a framework that advances multimodal learning and broadens its applicability to real-world biomedical problems.

title: Perioperative hemodynamic optimization.
source: PubMed · Current opinion in critical care
desc: [Current opinion in critical care] Perioperative hemodynamic optimization using goal-directed therapy (GDT) reduces complications and mortality in high-risk surgery. This review synthesizes advances over the last few years, focusing on dynamic physiological targets, predictive artificial intelligence, microcirculatory and endothelial protection, individualized arterial pressure targets, volume stewardship and novel nonadrenergic rescue vasopressors for postcardiopulmonary bypass vasoplegia, and extracorporeal blood purification for refractory vasoplegia in surgical sepsis. Clinical practice has shifted from rigid volumetric protocols toward individualized physiological stewardship and endothelial glycocalyx preservation, framed within the four-phase dynamic continuum (ROSE concept: Resuscitation, Optimization, Stabilization, and Evacuation). Machine-learning algorithms, such as the Hypotension Prediction Index, effectively preempt intraoperative hypotension. Point-of-care ultrasound protocols, notably the venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) score, prevent backward venous congestion. Concurrently, dynamic arterial elastance (Eadyn) distinguishes between vasodilation and preload deficit. In cardiothoracic surgery, postcardiopulmonary bypass vasoplegia mandates cautious fluid restriction and early multimodal nonadrenergic vasopressors, including methylene blue, hydroxocobalamin (vitamin B12), and synthetic angiotensin II, which effectively restore vascular tone and limit catecholamine toxicity. In surgical sepsis and refractory vasoplegic shock, blood purification therapies provide valuable hemodynamic rescue; the pioneer continuous hemodiafiltration with cytokine-adsorbing hemofilters (CAH-CHDF) and recent trial data with polymyxin B hemoperfusion (the TIGRIS trial) demonstrate significant vasopressor-sparing effects and restored vascular tone. Perioperative hemodynamic optimization has evolved into a multimodal, patient-tailored approach. Coupling dynamic fluid responsiveness with predictive monitoring, personalized blood pressure titration, nonadrenergic rescue for postbypass vasoplegic shock, organ venous congestion profiling, and extracorporeal humoral modulation provides comprehensive circulatory support while preventing fluid overload.

title: Advancements in Diabetic Retinopathy Classification Using Novel Multi-Stacked U-Net Architectures
desc: Diabetes leads to several health complications throughout the body, with the complication in the eyes being Diabetic Retinopathy. It leads to damaging or abnormal changes in the blood vessels' structure, causing vision loss. The need for massive screening of a large population of diabetic patients has created a necessity for computer-aided, fully automatic diagnosis of DR. CNNs have shown great promise in the classification of DR based on the Fundus images. Building a reliable model faces considerable challenges due to the limited availability of high-quality annotated datasets and issues with varying image quality and class imbalances. This paper aims to demonstrate the UNET, and its Stacked Architecture variant and their performance across several datasets. This paper has compared and studied the UNET architecture's performance across multiple stacks and has come to a soft conclusion that the architecture performs its best at three stacks, and any more leads to deterioration of its performance. The model aims at classifying the images into five categories, 0 to 4, where 0 is no DR, and 4 is proliferative DR.

title: A multilingual mobile application for digital mental health support, emotional tracking, and therapist interaction.
desc: [Frontiers in digital health] Depression and other mental health challenges can affect daily functioning and well-being, while social stigma and limited access to culturally appropriate digital resources may discourage individuals from seeking support. This study presents REWAA, a bilingual mobile application designed to support emotional self-tracking, access to mental health resources, and interaction with mental health professionals in Arabic and English. REWAA was developed as an Android application with separate patient and therapist interfaces. Its features include mood self-tracking, an exploratory AI-based facial-analysis tool, the Bilingual Hybrid Mood Heuristic (BHMH) protocol, an AI-supported conversational tool, mental wellness resources, peer support groups, and therapist communication. The application was evaluated through a user survey involving 200 respondents to assess usability, perceived usefulness, emotional awareness, privacy, and user acceptance. Survey responses indicated generally positive perceptions of REWAA. Most respondents rated the graphical user interface as comfortable and easy to navigate (70%), while 60% reported that the REWAA bot helped them better understand their feelings and provided practical advice. In addition, 55% reported a significant improvement in emotional awareness, and 65% considered the application useful alongside professional therapy. Overall, the findings indicate positive user perceptions of the application's accessibility and integrated support features. REWAA demonstrates the potential of a bilingual digital platform to bring emotional self-tracking, supportive resources, and therapist interaction together in one application. However, the findings primarily reflect user-reported usability and acceptance and do not establish clinical diagnostic accuracy or therapeutic effectiveness. Further evaluation involving appropriate clinical validation and longitudinal follow-up is needed to assess its effectiveness and reliability in real-world mental health settings.

title: TriSegAgent: Context-Efficient 3D Annotation with MLLMs via Tri-Planes
desc: Interactive segmentation models turn a few clicks into a segmentation prediction across domains, so annotators only decide where the prediction still needs correction. Annotation thus becomes a loop of inspecting the prediction and clicking again. Each step of this loop is a visual judgment, which suits general-purpose multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents. In this work, we focus on letting these agents run this loop on 3D volumes. However, the MLLM in such an agent takes only 2D images as input, so the agent must observe the 3D volume in 2D. Since the loop calls the MLLM many times, this observation must be token-compact enough to keep every call cheap, yet informative enough to show error regions in the 3D prediction. We meet both needs with tri-planes, the three orthogonal planes that cross at one point in the volume. We show, both theoretically and empirically, that tri-planes are context-efficient yet keep sufficient detail to show error regions in the 3D prediction. Building on tri-planes, we introduce TriSegAgent, an MLLM agent that refines the 3D prediction iteratively. Within the agent, the MLLM only judges the prediction on tri-planes, while a visual harness turns each judgment into a 3D action in code. To make the loop reliable, the harness places each click at an exact voxel in the volume and checks whether to accept the 3D prediction. To evaluate the agent, we build a diverse benchmark of 690 regions of interest (ROIs) from 35 public medical datasets across three imaging modalities. With frontier MLLMs, TriSegAgent reaches an overall Dice about 10 points above the strongest baseline, and its lead is even larger on targets below 3 cm. With flash-level MLLMs, it outperforms a recent 3D segmentation agent built on a frontier MLLM.

title: System of agentic AI for the discovery of metal-organic frameworks.
desc: [Nature computational science] Generative models and machine learning promise accelerated material discovery in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 capture and water harvesting, but face substantial challenges in navigating vast chemical spaces while ensuring synthesizability. Here we present MOFGen, a system of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) comprising interconnected agents: a large language model that proposes MOF compositions, a diffusion model that generates crystal structures, quantum mechanical agents that optimize and filter candidates, and synthetic-feasibility agents guided by expert rules and machine learning. Trained on a broad set of experimentally reported MOFs and computational databases, MOFGen generated hundreds of thousands of MOF structures and synthesizable organic linkers. The uniqueness of our approach lies in its ability to generate large MOF structures with atomic precision, beyond the scale of conventional generative models limited to tens of atoms. This approach was validated through high-throughput experiments and the successful synthesis of four 'AI-dreamt' MOFs.

title: Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields with Bidirectional Diffusion Encoders for Zero-Training Cross-Ontology Medical Coding
desc: Healthcare systems continually revise clinical taxonomies, update reimbursement schedules, and harmonize cross-border registries. Existing automated coding models bind clinical text understanding to fixed vocabulary-specific heads, requiring manual relabeling and retraining whenever code sets change. We introduce Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields (OCSF), a vocabulary-free framework that decouples clinical document reading from target ontology indexing so one trained encoder can switch across arbitrary medical vocabularies in seconds without target training. A single-pass bidirectional diffusion-pretrained encoder and vocabulary-free decoder map each clinical note into a fixed-dimension two-dimensional state matrix with zero code-specific parameters. Any target ontology is compiled offline on CPU from public text descriptions into a scale-invariant Tikhonov deconvolution operator that suppresses sibling-code interference while preserving source decision thresholds. Trained solely on English MIMIC-IV ICD-9 discharge summaries and evaluated without target tuning across 58,706 held-out test notes and five unseen ontologies spanning English ICD-10, MS-DRG, Spanish, Greek, and Chinese (115-185,458 codes), OCSF reaches 63.15% Micro-F1 on in-domain ICD-9 (outperforming a matched closed-vocabulary classifier and eliminating late-epoch tail overfitting) and transfers directly to 26,085 English ICD-10 codes (29.23% recall at gold cardinality), MS-DRG groups, and multilingual terminologies, compiling up to 185,458 codes in under 10 seconds on CPU with sub-millisecond GPU readout.

title: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for epilepsy.
desc: [Progress in brain research] Epilepsy is among the most burdensome neurological disorders worldwide, with an impact that extends far beyond seizure frequency alone. Depression, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and internalized stigma affect a substantial proportion of individuals with epilepsy, yet these comorbidities remain systematically undertreated in routine neurological care. Conventional psychoeducation, largely centered on passive information delivery, has shown limited effectiveness in addressing the psychological and social complexities of living with epilepsy. Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation for Epilepsy (NIPE) offers a fundamentally different approach: one that translates the neuroscience of seizure generation, network dysfunction, and neuroplasticity into accessible frameworks, shifting patients from passive recipients of information to active, metacognitively engaged participants in their own care. This chapter presents NIPE as both a clinical framework and an integrative layer across the continuum of epilepsy management. Beginning with the neurobiological mechanisms underlying seizures and epileptogenesis, it highlights how the same neural networks implicated in ictal activity also contribute to the psychiatric and cognitive comorbidities that shape patients' daily experiences. It further examines how NIPE interfaces with evidence-based psychological interventions, pharmacologic education, neuromodulation, epilepsy surgery, and the management of refractory epilepsy, as well as the unique needs of women and other populations with distinct clinical considerations. In addition, the chapter explores the digital expansion of NIPE, including adaptive telehealth platforms, wearable biosensors, digital phenotyping, and the emerging role of artificial intelligence in tailoring psychoeducational delivery. Importantly, it addresses current limitations and ethical considerations with transparency, including the absence of standardized NIPE protocols and the relative scarcity of randomized controlled trials specifically within epilepsy populations. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking perspective on the infrastructure, research agenda, and cross-disciplinary collaboration required to embed NIPE into routine epileptology practice. NIPE is positioned not as an adjunct to epilepsy care, but as a unifying framework, a shared language that enables truly integrated, patient-centered care.

title: PathStream: Towards Streaming Diagnostic Copilots for Whole-Slide Pathology
desc: Pathologists reach a diagnosis by integrating morphological evidence across regions and magnifications along viewing trajectories. Existing pathology AI rarely reflects this process: models predict from selected image regions, answer questions within fixed visual contexts, or navigate slides autonomously. We formalize pathologist-led streaming diagnosis, in which the pathologist controls navigation while a copilot selectively describes incoming views and synthesizes accumulated evidence into a final diagnosis. We record five pathologists' viewing trajectories on 1,791 TCGA whole-slide images (WSIs) spanning ten organs, with response labels, morphological descriptions, and session-level findings and diagnoses. We construct PathStreamBench to assess response timing, morphological description, and session-level diagnosis, alongside auxiliary video understanding. We introduce PathStream, which jointly learns streaming responses and diagnosis through two-stage training, with a diagnosis-attention loss guiding attention during diagnosis to relevant visual and textual evidence accumulated as the examination unfolds. PathStream outperforms 14 vision-language models and three domain-fine-tuned baselines on the core tasks, achieving a trajectory WSI Relevance score of 77.87, surpassing the strongest domain-fine-tuned baseline's 62.76. Without additional training, its diagnostic capabilities generalize to new educational pathology videos, three external centers, and an unseen organ.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Aided Design of Peptides with Custom Secondary Structure Motifs and Reduced Amino Acid Alphabets.
source: PubMed · Journal of chemical information and modeling
desc: [Journal of chemical information and modeling] Proteins are highly diverse functional polymers where the specific sequence of amino acids, selected from a standard genetically encoded alphabet of 20 (C20), determines the structure and ultimately the function of the resulting folded protein. This standard alphabet has been identified to be nonrandomly distributed in physicochemical properties crucial to both structure formation and function, often referred to as coverage theory. While machine learning models have drastically improved protein structure prediction, success of protein design models lags structure prediction, particularly for custom secondary structure motifs and amino acid alphabets. Here, we therefore bridge contemporary biological theory with recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) to develop and evaluate a generative AI protein design model, trained on hundreds of thousands of proteins within the RCSB PDB, for custom secondary structure motifs using reduced amino acid alphabets (RAAs). Results indicate an overall success in designing novel proteins with desired secondary structure motifs for a broad range of amino acid alphabets and complexity of designs. Interestingly, for a substantial fraction of designs, ESMFold predicts a fold close to that of the target structure despite training only on physicochemical sequence space and secondary structure information. The development of this model advances research across multiple disciplines, from general scientific AI architecture development to protein design for biotechnology, astrobiology, and early-Earth evolutionary biology.

title: Rethinking Closed-Ended Medical VLM Evaluation: From Stable Wrongness to Counterfactual Answer Sensitivity
desc: As medical VLMs are increasingly evaluated for clinical decision-support scenarios, knowing when to trust their predictions is critical. Closed-ended medical VQA has become a common benchmark format because it enables automated scoring. Yet, systematic investigation into whether this format changes the reliability problem remains scarce. We identify a failure mode that we call stable wrongness: models can produce incorrect yes/no answers that remain confident and repeatable even when patient-specific visual evidence is removed or mismatched. This failure violates the premise behind sampling-stability uncertainty methods, including recent hallucination-aware calibration (HAC) variants: disagreement is informative only when errors are unstable. When shortcut-driven errors are themselves stable, sampling agreement can remain deceptively high. Motivated by this limitation, we introduce Counterfactual Answer Sensitivity (CAS), which shifts reliability estimation from answer stability to evidence sensitivity. CAS uses cross-modal counterfactual interventions, such as text-only, black, and corrupted images, to audit whether a committed yes/no answer remains supported when visual evidence is invalidated. Across 7 VLMs and 3 benchmarks, CAS outperforms the best HAC-family scores across all evaluated settings, achieving a macro-averaged AUROC gain of +0.150 for error detection. Mechanistic analysis further shows that CAS recovers hidden errors in the HAC-confident region and that its strongest standalone signal is counterfactual decision-boundary shift rather than hard prediction stability. Our findings suggest that closed-ended evaluation should test visual dependence, not only answer stability, in safety-critical medical contexts.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Nanozymes: From Design to Application.
desc: [Advanced healthcare materials] Nanozymes are synthetic nanomaterials engineered to mimic the catalytic functions of natural enzymes, characterized by facile synthesis, ease of surface modification, low cost, and high stability, and they have been widely applied in various fields. However, the rational design and synthesis of nanozymes remain complex, and their activity is challenging to predict. In recent years, the advent of machine learning (ML) has shown great promise in addressing these issues. This review first systematically elucidates the fundamental principles and common algorithms of ML, followed by an exploration of its role in nanozyme research, with a focused discussion on the synergistic applications of ML and nanozymes in the biomedical field. Finally, this review analyzes the key challenges faced by researchers in applying ML to nanozyme studies as well as the corresponding solutions and provides an outlook on future development directions. Furthermore, given the relatively limited reports on ML-assisted nanozyme research to date, this study aims to deepen the understanding of nanozymes and more effectively advance nanozyme research toward the era of artificial intelligence.

title: Exploring Attention-Driven Deep Learning for Accurate Lung Nodule Segmentation
desc: This study explores the application of various deep learning models for the segmentation of lung nodules using LIDC-IDRI. Unlike traditional approaches that utilize the full dataset, our work emphasizes the efficacy of training models on a filtered subset of 356 samples. Novel configurations, including attention mechanisms and advanced preprocessing strategies, were employed to optimize segmentation accuracy. Among the models evaluated, the DPL nkNet50 with a Channel Attention Bridge and ResNet backbone demonstrated the highest performance with a Dice score of 0.86, significantly outperforming conventional architectures. This work underscores the potential of leveraging data efficiency and tailored architectures in achieving robust segmentation performance, paving the way for improved computer-aided diagnosis in clinical settings.

title: From Hallucinations to Uncertainty: The Next Challenge for Clinical AI.
source: PubMed · Journal of medical Internet research
desc: [Journal of medical Internet research] Clinical AI continues to improve, but are existing models truly ready for the clinic? In this News and Perspectives article, JMIR Correspondent Elena Ikonomovska reports on the evolution of clinical AI evaluation, sharing her opinion on the next frontier that large language models must reach in order to support holistic, effective clinical care.

title: SleepXA: Composing Pretrained Neural and Cardiac Foundation Models for Sleep Representation Learning
desc: Physiological signals recorded during sleep provide synchronized views of neural, cardiac, respiratory, and other bodily systems, while preserving modality-specific information. Existing EEG and ECG foundation models already capture rich but distinct physiological structure, motivating an alternative to training a multimodal sleep model from scratch: composing existing pretrained models. We introduce SleepXA, a framework that uses synchronized polysomnography (PSG) to compose independently pretrained neural and cardiac foundation models. SleepXA combines pretrained EEG and ECG encoders with lightweight encoders for additional PSG modalities, and learns shared and modality-specific representations through sleep-guided alignment. We pretrain SleepXA on 9,230 overnight PSG recordings from three large cohorts and evaluate it on 27 downstream tasks spanning sleep representation, clinical and disease prediction, and daytime physiological transfer. SleepXA ranks among the top two methods on 22 of 27 tasks. Controlled experiments further show consistent benefits across sensor configurations and EEG-ECG backbone choices, while pretrained initialization outperforms architecture-matched training from scratch and SleepXA surpasses alternative multimodal composition strategies. These results suggest that synchronized multimodal physiology can serve as a natural interface for composing existing physiological foundation models, yielding reusable representations that extend beyond sleep to clinical and daytime physiological settings.

title: Wearable automated cough detection in horses with chronic cough: model development, validation, and exploratory associations in asthma.
source: PubMed · Journal of veterinary internal medicine
desc: [Journal of veterinary internal medicine] Coughing is a nonspecific respiratory sign that is common in horses with asthma. Cough quantification is currently subjective and labor-intensive, leaving its diagnostic and monitoring potential underexplored. (1) Develop a wearable audio recorder for horses; (2) collect recordings of coughing horses and annotate coughs; (3) train a machine learning model to automate cough detection; and (4) describe temporal patterns of coughing and determine pathophysiologic correlations in horses with asthma. Seventy horses were recruited from a teaching herd, clinical cases, and via social media. Sixty had coughing for ≥3 weeks and valid recordings. In our prospective observational and analytical study, coughs were recorded using a digital device, annotated by a single observer, and used to develop a machine-learning-based cough-detection pipeline. Machine learning output was analyzed using generalized linear mixed models to determine circadian patterns and pathophysiologic associations of coughing. We annotated 252 of 1260 recorded hours. We labeled 8555 sound events, 2780 of which were coughs of the instrumented horse. Our machine learning model detected coughs with a sensitivity of 0.95 and a specificity of 0.9993. In horses with asthma, coughing frequency was associated with neutrophilic lung inflammation and showed a diurnal pattern with peak rates around 3 am. The combination of robust hardware for long-term recordings and high-performance machine learning algorithms has the potential to transform coughing from a relatively crude clinical sign to a quantifiable endpoint in research and clinical practice.

title: Pain Reassessment from Pulse Waveforms with Language Model Explanations
desc: Routine photoplethysmography (PPG) offers a continuous physiological signal for pain reassessment between self-reports. Whether prior recordings provide an individualized physiological reference beyond care-process timing remains unresolved. Across 52,082 report-linked assessments from 21,514 patients in MIMIC-III critical care and MC-MED emergency care, we evaluate a workflow that pairs longitudinal PPG representations with local evidence-linked language interpretation. Among 27 methods, source-selected full-history models achieved average precision of 0.824 from critical to emergency care and 0.822 in reverse. Removing historical pulse-run representations while retaining reassessment availability and elapsed time lowered critical-to-emergency four-hour within-patient concordance from 0.718 to 0.534. This comparison supports the contribution of prior pulse-run representations to within-patient ordering beyond timing cues. Across 2,905 test patients, a local Qwen model interpreting frozen predictions achieved a 94.7% patient-equal pass rate on automated evidence checks after at most one revision. Longitudinal pulse context and evidence-linked language interpretation support a patient-centred workflow for pain reassessment.

title: The effectiveness of AI-based cognitive behavioral therapy chatbots for anxiety and depression symptoms: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] AI chatbots are increasingly being used to provide accessible psychological support. However, the effectiveness of chatbot-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety and depressive symptoms remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of artificial intelligence chatbot-based cognitive behavioral therapy on anxiety and depressive symptoms. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wanfang, and CBM databases was conducted from their inception to July 8th, 2025. Updated search on August 25, 2026. Meta-analysis was conducted using Stata version 18.0 and RevMan version 5.4. The ES for the treatment effect was calculated using the SMD. Ten studies involving a total of 1,301 participants. The results of the meta-analysis showed that the CBT of AI chatbots could significantly improve depressive symptoms at the end of the intervention (d = -0.40, 95% CI: -0.62 ~ -0.17, P = 0.0005). In contrast, the intervention did not significantly improve anxiety symptoms (d = -0.029, 95% CI: -0.145 ~ 0.087, P = 0.623), with no substantial heterogeneity detected (I 2= 0%). The subgroup analysis for depressive symptoms indicated significant effects were observed in participant age stratification, intervention Duration, and Control group intervention. However, some subgroup estimates were based on a small number of studies, so the data should be interpreted with caution. This meta-analysis emphasizes that AI-based chatbots for CBT may have great potential in contributing to the alleviation of depressive symptoms. Given the small number of included studies and the high heterogeneity, the results should be interpreted with caution. More high-quality RCTs are needed in the future to further validate these findings and explore their long-term benefits. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251089835.

title: Diagnosing Verbalized Confidence in a Medical Vision-Language Model for Selective Prediction on Colorectal Histopathology Patches
desc: Flagging uncertain histopathology patches for specialist review needs a confidence that is higher when the model is right. We test whether an open medical vision-language model emits one. MedGemma-27b-it and its base Gemma-3-27b-it were run zero-shot under one prompt on 10,004 PathMNIST validation patches and 7,180 patches of a patient-disjoint external cohort. Both are too inaccurate to deploy (40.6% and 35.5%); the object of study is the confidence. MedGemma's verbalized confidence puts 96% of patches at one value; its confidence-correctness AUROC is 0.499 and 0.528, and routing by it moves selective-accuracy AUC by -0.004 and +0.037. Gemma-3 spreads its confidence over nine values, reaches AUROC 0.70, and gains +0.114 and +0.115. MedGemma's label-token probabilities do not rescue it: their validation advantage reverses where the top-20 alternatives include every class. On 1,800-patch subsets of each cohort, stratified on correctness and reweighted to the full splits, agreement across five prompt variants beats random by +0.123 and +0.106, and wording-only paraphrases give +0.100 and, externally and in direction only, +0.054; agreement's external margins over confidence do not survive slide-level clustering. Under one restructured prompt variant, MedGemma's stated confidence routes (+0.112, +0.141), so the failure is tied to a prompt chosen for macro F1.

title: BlindDDG: A Blind Evaluation-Based Method for Protein Mutation Stability Prediction.
source: PubMed · Journal of chemical information and modeling
desc: [Journal of chemical information and modeling] Protein thermodynamic stability changes upon mutation profoundly affect protein structure and biological function. Recent advances in deep learning and protein language models have provided powerful tools for computational analysis of mutation-induced stability changes. However, most existing methods focus on quantitative regression of free-energy changes, which places strong dependence on precise experimentally measured ΔΔG values, although reliably determining the direction of stability change is itself an important objective in many practical applications. Here, we propose BlindDDG, a novel framework that reformulates protein mutation stability prediction from quantitative ΔΔG estimation to direction-oriented stability change classification. First, we introduce a blind-evaluation strategy that models mutation-induced changes by learning the representation difference between wild-type and mutant proteins, rather than relying solely on their individual intrinsic properties. This formulation focuses on the direction of stability changes and reduces the dependence on precise quantitative ΔΔG measurements. Second, a Siamese architecture with shared parameters is employed to encode the wild-type and mutant states and capture subtle mutation-associated differences. Third, a local structure-aware cross-attention mechanism is developed to integrate mutation-centered structural information with global protein language model representations, enabling effective multimodal feature interaction. Experimental results on the independent S669 benchmark demonstrate that BlindDDG achieves strong classification performance, obtaining an F1 score of 0.5449, an MCC of 0.3929, an accuracy of 0.7721, and a recall of 0.5417 for stabilizing mutation identification. BlindDDG outperforms all evaluated methods in F1 score, MCC, accuracy, and recall, highlighting its effectiveness in capturing mutation-induced stability changes, particularly for imbalanced stability classification.

title: SignalCount: Approximate Counts with Structured and Semantic Predicates in Seconds
desc: Many applications store records with structured columns and a text document, and ask how many records in a filtered set meet a criterion that only a reader of the text can judge, such as "How many patients with type 2 diabetes, aged 40 to 70, stopped metformin because their blood sugar stayed high?"
